modules.title: Introduction to Drone Technology
modules.summary: Start here — the basics of what a drone is and how it stays in the air.

sections.heading: What is a drone?
sections.body: A drone — formally an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) — is an aircraft that flies without a pilot on board. It's controlled remotely by a person on the ground, or it flies partly or fully on its own using onboard computers.

sections.heading: How drones work
sections.body: A drone combines four things working together: a structure to hold everything (the frame), motors and propellers to generate lift and movement, a flight controller that acts as the 'brain' making thousands of tiny corrections per second, and a power source to run it all. Pilot commands — or pre-programmed instructions — tell the flight controller what to do, and it translates that into precise motor speed changes.

sections.heading: Common applications
sections.body: Drones are used for aerial photography and film, precision agriculture, infrastructure inspection, land surveying and mapping, search and rescue, package delivery, and scientific research. We cover these in more depth in the Applications module.

sections.heading: Basic terminology
sections.body: A few terms you'll see throughout Dronova: UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle), FPV (First Person View — flying using a live video feed), payload (anything extra the drone carries, like a camera), telemetry (live data sent back from the drone), and flight controller (the onboard computer that stabilizes and controls flight).

terms.def: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle — an aircraft with no pilot on board.
First Person View — flying using a live video feed from the aircraft.
Extra equipment a drone carries, such as a camera or sensor.
Live flight data (altitude, speed, battery, GPS) sent from the drone to the pilot.

modules.title: Types of Drones
modules.summary: Three major drone categories, each suited to different missions.

droneTypes.name: Multirotor
droneTypes.desc: Uses multiple fixed-pitch propellers (usually 4, 6, or 8) to generate lift and control. Steers purely by varying each motor's speed independently — no moving control surfaces.

droneTypes.name: Fixed-Wing
droneTypes.desc: Shaped like a small airplane, with a rigid wing that generates lift as it moves forward. Cannot hover, and needs airspeed to stay aloft.

droneTypes.name: VTOL
droneTypes.desc: Vertical Take-Off and Landing fixed-wing — combines a multirotor's ability to take off and land vertically with a fixed-wing's efficient forward flight, usually by tilting rotors or using separate lift/cruise propulsion.
useCases: Search and rescue over large areas

modules.title: How a Drone Flies
modules.summary: The four core forces, and the three ways a drone rotates.

forces.name: Thrust
forces.desc: The forward or upward force generated by the spinning propellers. Thrust must exceed weight for the drone to climb.

forces.name: Lift
forces.desc: On a multirotor, lift comes directly from thrust pointed upward. On a fixed-wing, lift comes from air moving over the wing shape.

forces.name: Weight
forces.desc: The downward force of gravity acting on the drone's total mass — frame, battery, motors, and payload all add to it.

forces.name: Drag
forces.desc: Air resistance opposing the drone's motion — the faster or less aerodynamic the shape, the more drag it must overcome.

axes.name: Pitch
axes.desc: Tilting nose-up or nose-down, moving the drone forward or backward. Achieved by speeding up motors on one side and slowing the opposite side.

axes.name: Roll
axes.desc: Tilting left or right, moving the drone sideways. Achieved the same way as pitch, but along the perpendicular axis.

axes.name: Yaw
axes.desc: Rotating around the vertical axis, like turning on the spot. Achieved by spinning clockwise-turning motors faster or slower than counter-clockwise ones, exploiting the torque difference.

controls.name: Throttle
controls.desc: Controls the drone's vertical movement. Increasing throttle causes the drone to gain altitude, while decreasing throttle causes it to descend — it works by increasing the thrust each propeller generates.

controls.name: Pitch
controls.desc: Tilts the drone forward or backward and controls forward/backward movement, by speeding up motors on one side and slowing the opposite side.

controls.name: Roll
controls.desc: Tilts the drone left or right and controls lateral (sideways) movement, using the same speed-difference technique as pitch along the perpendicular axis.

controls.name: Yaw
controls.desc: Rotates the drone around its vertical axis, changing which way it faces, by exploiting the torque difference between clockwise and counter-clockwise spinning motors.

modules.title: Drone Applications
modules.summary: Real-world industries where drones are already changing how work gets done.

apps.name: Aerial Photography & Film
apps.desc: Capturing angles and moving shots that would otherwise need a helicopter or crane.

apps.name: Agriculture
apps.desc: Monitoring crop health, spraying fields precisely, and tracking irrigation needs from the air.

apps.name: Infrastructure Inspection
apps.desc: Examining bridges, towers, power lines, and pipelines without putting a person at height or in danger.

apps.name: Mapping & Surveying
apps.desc: Generating precise aerial maps and 3D terrain models far faster than traditional ground surveying.

apps.name: Search & Rescue
apps.desc: Covering large or difficult terrain quickly with thermal cameras to locate missing persons.

apps.name: Logistics & Delivery
apps.desc: Delivering small packages directly to homes or remote areas, bypassing road congestion.

apps.name: Research & Science
apps.desc: Studying wildlife, weather patterns, and environmental change with minimal disturbance to the subject.

apps.name: Aerospace Exploration
apps.desc: Testing autonomous flight and control systems that inform both terrestrial drones and next-generation aircraft.
